The '''Well of the Dark Side''' was a location on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Mortis/Legends|Mortis]] where all the energies of the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]] in the universe were channeled into the bottom of a volcanic crater.

==History==
The [[Son/Legends|Son]] resided here, where he drew his strength in the dark side of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]. Upon learning that the Son was planning to escape Mortis (an act that ultimately would defy a cardinal planetary law by which [[The Ones/Legends|the Ones]]—[[Father (Mortis)/Legends|Father]], Son and [[Daughter]]—were bound, resulting in a catastrophic imbalance in the Force), [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] followed the instructions of the [[Force ghost/Legends|ghost]] of [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] to go to the Well. After riding his [[Speeder bike/Legends|speeder bike]] to the bottom of the Well, Skywalker encountered the Son. Shaken by the Son's [[Force vision/Legends|vision]] of the future that was shown him (not unlike Anakin's disturbing [[Holt Kazed]] cave vision antecedent to the [[Battle of Nelvaan]] in which he glimpsed his own monstrous future), the young [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] willingly followed the Force's dark-side embodiment in order to avoid realization of the Son's heinous, premeditated act. By the time [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] rode his own speeder bike to the bottom of the Well, Kenobi could only watch in horror as Skywalker left the sanctum of the Well to take his place alongside the Son, who was intent still on leaving Mortis (the planet symbolizing universal creation). Fortunately, [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]] arrived on her own speeder bike to pick up the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] and pursue, for all three Jedi, a route to ultimate rescue from the visionary realm, as well as (albeit through death of the Ones) a preservation of balance in the Force.

==Behind the scenes==
The Well of the Dark Side was introduced in the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' third season episode "[[Ghosts of Mortis]]."

At first, the fiery location's concept shares similarities where a [[Duel on Mustafar/Legends|showdown]] on the planet [[Mustafar/Legends|Mustafar]] occurs in [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']]. However, the primary concept's inspiration is from [[Ralph McQuarrie]]'s sketches of [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker's]] showdown with [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] and Darth Vader within the [[Imperial Palace/Legends|Imperial Palace's]] subterranean levels on the planet [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] (until [[Battle of Endor/Legends|the showdown]] was changed to the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]] in [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']]).<ref name="epguide">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode317.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Ghosts of Mortis}}</ref>
